title: Cardiac Action Potential Protocol
author: Robert Harvey
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ba8qihvw

steps.title: Prepare extracellular bathing solution
steps.instruction: Prepare extracellular solution containing (in mM): NaCl 140, KCl 5.4, CaCl₂ 2.5, MgCl₂ 0.5, glucose 5.5, HEPES 5; adjust pH to 7.4 and warm to 37 °C.

steps.title: Place cells in perfusion chamber
steps.instruction: Transfer isolated pig ventricular myocytes to a perfusion chamber on the stage of an inverted microscope and superfuse with the prepared extracellular solution at 37 °C.

steps.title: Fill pipette with intracellular solution
steps.instruction: Prepare intracellular solution containing (in mM): K‑aspartate 110, KCl 25, NaCl 5, MgATP 3, cAMP 0.002, phosphocreatine dipotassium 10, EGTA 0.01, HEPES 10; adjust pH to 7.2, and fill patch‑clamp microelectrodes (resistance 1–2 MΩ).

steps.title: Establish whole‑cell configuration
steps.instruction: Using the filled microelectrodes, obtain a gigaseal and transition to whole‑cell mode on the isolated myocytes.

steps.title: Set recording parameters
steps.instruction: Record membrane potential under current‑clamp using a Multiclamp 700B amplifier, Digidata 1440A interface, and pClamp 11 software; low‑pass filter at 4 kHz and sample at 10 kHz.

steps.title: Verify cell suitability
steps.instruction: Confirm resting membrane potential ≤ ‑75 mV, ensure stimulus artifact does not overlap the upstroke, and obtain a stable baseline for ~5 minutes; discard cells failing any criterion.

steps.title: Elicit action potentials
steps.instruction: Apply a 2 ms depolarizing stimulus every 5 s, adjusting amplitude to approximately 1.2 × the minimum voltage required to trigger an action potential.

steps.title: Acquire baseline data
steps.instruction: Collect baseline recordings for about 5 minutes before adding any test drugs.
